title: Ontem descansei — the past tense of regular verbs
title_target: Como correu o fim de semana?
goal: Talk about things that have already happened. Portuguese verbs change not only with the subject but also with the **time** — and the past tense packs both into a single ending.
bekal: forming the past tense for the three groups of regular verbs
using past time expressions: *ontem*, *na semana passada*, *há dois dias*

dialogs.title: Diálogo — Segunda-feira de manhã
dialogs.intro: Monday morning at school. Ana wants to know how Budi's weekend went.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.text: Bom dia! Como correu o fim de semana?
lines.id: Good morning! How was your weekend?
lines.literal: good day! how ran the end of week?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Correu bem! No sábado acordei tarde e não saí de casa.
lines.id: It went well! On Saturday I woke up late and didn't leave the house.
lines.literal: it-ran well! on-the Saturday I-woke late and not I-went-out of house.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Descansei. À tarde estudei um pouco e telefonei à minha mãe.
lines.id: I did. In the afternoon I studied a bit and called my mother.
lines.literal: I-rested. at-the afternoon I-studied a little and I-phoned to-the my mother.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: No domingo a dona Fernanda convidou-me para almoçar.
lines.id: On Sunday Mrs. Fernanda invited me to lunch.
lines.literal: on-the Sunday the lady Fernanda invited-me for to-lunch.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.id: How kind! What did you eat?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Comemos bacalhau. Ela cozinhou a tarde toda.
lines.id: We had salt cod. She cooked all afternoon.
lines.literal: we-ate cod. she cooked the afternoon whole.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Adorei! Comi demais e depois dormi duas horas.
lines.id: I loved it! I ate too much and then slept for two hours.
lines.literal: I-adored! I-ate too-much and after I-slept two hours.

lines.speaker: Ana:
lines.text: E eu que estudei o fim de semana inteiro...
lines.id: And here I was, studying all weekend...
lines.literal: and I who I-studied the end of week entire...

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Coitada! Mas já acabou. Hoje descansas.
lines.id: Poor you! But it's over now. Today you rest.
lines.literal: poor(f)! but already it-ended. today you-rest.

notes: **Como correu?** is the Portuguese way of asking "how did it go?" — for exams, job interviews, weekends, anything. The verb is *correr* (to run), so literally "how did it run?". The answer uses the same verb: *Correu bem* or *Correu mal*.
**Convidou-me** — the pronoun still attaches after the verb, just like in the present. The puller rule still applies too: *não me convidou*, *quem te convidou?*

**Comeram o quê?** Note *o quê* with an accent at the end of the sentence. The question word *que* takes an accent when it stands at the end of a sentence or on its own: *O quê?* ("what?"), but *O que é que comeram?* at the start.
**Já acabou** = "it's over now". *Já* with the past tense marks something as truly finished, like English "already".
**Saí, with an accent.** The verb *sair* has an accent in the *eu* and *tu* past forms: *saí*, *saíste*. The accent tells you that *a* and *i* are pronounced separately, not as one gliding sound.
**Inteiro and todo** both mean "whole". *A tarde toda* and *a tarde inteira* are the same; the first is said more often.

grammars.title: Past tense: -ar verbs
body: This form is used for actions that are **finished** and clearly bounded — yesterday, last week, last year. For past habits, Portuguese has another form that isn't part of A1.
after: **Falámos with an accent — this is the European spelling.** Present *falamos* and past *falámos* are written differently and pronounced differently: the first with a short, closed *a*, the second with an open, long *a*. In Brazil both forms are written the same (*falamos*), so context has to tell them apart. This module uses the European spelling.

**The *ele* form ends in -ou and is pronounced "oh", not "ow".** *Falou* = fuh-LOH, *comprou* = kohn-PROH, *cozinhou* = koo-zee-NYOH. This is the past ending you'll hear most, because people talk about other people more often.

grammars.title: Past tense: -er and -ir verbs
body: As in the present, the two are almost identical. This time the only difference is in the *eu* form.
after: **The *nós* form for -er and -ir is exactly the same as the present:** *comemos* can mean "we eat" or "we ate". No accent helps here, so context decides — and in practice it's never confusing, because a time expression is almost always mentioned.

grammars.title: Past time expressions
body: Almost every past-tense sentence carries one of these. Saying it makes your sentence clear even when your verb form isn't perfect yet.
after: **Há means "ago" when paired with the past tense**, and "for (so long)" when paired with the present. Compare: *cheguei há dois dias* (I arrived two days ago) and *estou aqui há dois meses* (I've been here for two months). One word, two jobs, and the verb form decides which.

sections.title: The regular verbs you'll use most in stories

blocks.text: **Cheguei with a u.** Verbs ending in *-gar* insert a *u* in the *eu* form to keep the hard sound: *chegar* → *cheguei*, *pagar* → *paguei*, *jogar* → *joguei*. Likewise *-car* becomes *-quei*: *ficar* → *fiquei*, *explicar* → *expliquei*. It's a spelling change, not a sound change.

blocks.title: One accent that marks two countries
items: Portugal writes **falámos**, **estudámos**, **comprámos** with an ´ accent for the past, and **falamos**, **estudamos** without it for the present.
Brazil writes both without the accent, because there the sounds aren't distinguished.
If you read a Brazilian text and see *falamos*, don't be confused — it could be present or past. In your own writing, follow the European spelling: the accent gives your reader a free clue.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct past-tense form.
items: Eu ____ a Lisboa há dois meses. (chegar)
We had salt cod on Sunday.

exercises.prompt: Spaced review — unit 12. Translate into Portuguese without looking back at the unit.

answers: Ontem falei com a Ana. — Na semana passada ela trabalhou muito. — No domingo comemos bacalhau. — Ontem estudaste português? — Anteontem eles chegaram às oito. — À tarde dormi duas horas.
acordei — cozinhou — descansámos — telefonaste — saíram — cheguei
Ontem estudei a tarde toda. — Como correu o fim de semana? — Comemos bacalhau no domingo. — Ela convidou-me para almoçar. — Cheguei há dois meses. — Dormi duas horas.
Levanto-me às sete. — Esqueço-me sempre das chaves. — Vejo-te amanhã! — Sinto-me mal. — Chamo-me Budi.
